payload.task_text:
I am a course coordinator and the Fall 2014 semester has just ended. I need your help wrapping up a few things. First, please look up our learning management system for all courses offered in Fall 2014. The course codes for that semester end with "2014J". For each of those courses, I need you to gather the total enrollment count and the average student score. The average student score is a per-student average: first compute each student's mean score across all of their non-null (graded) submission scores in the course, then average those per-student means across all students. Round this final value to two decimal places. I also need you to count how many regular assignments and how many quizzes each course had. Treat these as two mutually exclusive categories of assessments: a quiz is counted only under Quiz_Count, not also under Assignment_Count, so that no assessment is double-counted.

Second, I would like you to create an online feedback form for students to fill out. The form should be titled "Fall 2014 End-of-Semester Student Feedback". It needs five questions. The first question should ask "Which course are you providing feedback for?" and should be a multiple choice question listing all seven Fall 2014 courses as options, using the format "Course_Code: Course_Name" for each option. The second question should ask "Overall course satisfaction (1-5)" and should be a multiple choice question with the options 1 through 5. The third question should be a free text question asking "What did you like most about the course?" and the fourth should also be a free text question asking "What could be improved?". The fifth and final question should ask "Would you recommend this course to others?" and should be a multiple choice question with the options Yes, No, and Maybe.

Third, please compile all the course data into an Excel report saved as "Fall_2014_Course_Report.xlsx" in the workspace. The file should have a single sheet named "Course Statistics" with the following columns: Course_Code, Course_Name, Enrollment, Avg_Score, Assignment_Count, Quiz_Count, and Total_Assessments. The Avg_Score should be rounded to two decimal places. Total_Assessments is simply the sum of Assignment_Count and Quiz_Count. The rows should be sorted alphabetically by Course_Code. The Course_Name should be the short name without any semester suffix.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use exactly one parallel collector wave of seven per-course explore sub-agents that each compute their course's complete statistics outside the main context; the main agent itself creates the form and writes the workbook — no planning sub-agent, no second wave.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 7 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per literal Fall 2014 course below:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=2 (AAA-2014J). Follow this recipe once, aggregate after the terminal page, and return immediately — never re-read a page, re-run aggregation, or loop to re-verify: (1) Call canvas_get_course(course_id=2) once; record name, course_code, and total_students; SHORT NAME = name with the trailing " (Fall 2014)" removed. (2) Enrollment: call canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=2, type=["StudentEnrollment"], per_page=100, page=1..) following pagination.has_more, counting ALL returned enrollments regardless of enrollment_state. Record the enrolled user_id set. (3) Quiz_Count: call canvas_list_quizzes(course_id=2) once (including unpublished); count stable quiz IDs. (4) Assignment_Count: call canvas_list_assignments(course_id=2) once; count stable assignment IDs excluding any non-null quiz assignment_id. (5) Avg_Score: paginate canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=2, per_page=100, page=1..terminal) once per page stopping only at pagination.has_more=false, deduplicating stable row.id values; per-student mean over each student's non-null graded scores, then the mean across those per-student means rounded to two decimals (students with no graded submissions excluded). Return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id:2, course_code, short_name, enrollment, avg_score, assignment_count, quiz_count, graded_student_count, duplicate_submission_ids}; keep raw rows out of the main context and make no writes.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=4 (BBB-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=7 (CCC-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
   4. explore 3 (enterprise-data-analyst 3): Collector for course_id=10 (DDD-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
   5. explore 4 (enterprise-data-analyst 4): Collector for course_id=14 (EEE-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
   6. explore 5 (enterprise-data-analyst 5): Collector for course_id=17 (FFF-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
   7. explore 6 (enterprise-data-analyst 6): Collector for course_id=21 (GGG-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.

In the same response that launches Wave 1, the main agent calls create_form(title="Fall 2014 End-of-Semester Student Feedback") exactly once. After Wave 1 returns, on the retained form ID sequentially call add_multiple_choice_question titled `Which course are you providing feedback for?` with the exact options `AAA-2014J: Applied Analytics & Algorithms`, `BBB-2014J: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics`, `CCC-2014J: Creative Computing & Culture`, `DDD-2014J: Data-Driven Design`, `EEE-2014J: Environmental Economics & Ethics`, `FFF-2014J: Foundations of Finance`, and `GGG-2014J: Global Governance & Geopolitics`; add_multiple_choice_question titled `Overall course satisfaction (1-5)` with options `1`..`5`; add_text_question titled `What did you like most about the course?`; add_text_question titled `What could be improved?`; and add_multiple_choice_question titled `Would you recommend this course to others?` with options `Yes`, `No`, `Maybe`; then get_form(formId=<id>), retaining the verified ID/link and question order, and never retrying creation after an ambiguous failure.

After Wave 1 verify all seven handoffs in one single pass (one check, never a per-course iteration): exactly one handoff per manifest course, a present two-decimal avg_score, non-negative counts, and empty duplicate_submission_ids. Freeze exactly seven literal canonical rows with columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Enrollment, Avg_Score, Assignment_Count, Quiz_Count, Total_Assessments (= assignment_count + quiz_count), sorted by Course_Code.

The main agent then sole-writes <workspace_root>/Fall_2014_Course_Report.xlsx directly from the seven canonical rows — atomically, with only the `Course Statistics` sheet, the exact seven headers and seven code-sorted literal rows (all values literal numbers) — reads the populated range back, and verifies row count, headers and course codes. Accept only after the Excel and Form read-backs; no intermediate data is a final deliverable. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, and do not add a verification wave.

You are a planning sub-agent. Produce a detailed, ordered execution plan (do NOT execute any write operations — you only have read-only tools) for the following task. The workspace is /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-feedback/workspace. The available systems are a Canvas LMS (mcp__canvas__*), Google Forms (mcp__google_forms__*), Excel file manipulation (mcp__excel__*), and local filesystem (mcp__filesystem__* / mcp__local__python_execute). Note: course codes for Fall 2014 end with the suffix "2014J".

TASK (3 deliverables):

1) Canvas data gathering: Find ALL courses offered in Fall 2014 (course codes ending with "2014J"). For EACH such course, compute:
   - Total enrollment count (number of enrolled students).
   - Average student score: per-student average = for each student, mean of their non-null (graded) submission scores across all assessments in the course; then average those per-student means across ALL students; round final value to two decimal places. (Students with no graded submissions: decide how to treat them — recommend an approach, e.g. exclude from the average, and verify by exploring actual data.)
   - Assignment_Count: number of regular assignments (exclude quizzes from this count).
   - Quiz_Count: number of quizzes. Quizzes must be counted ONLY in Quiz_Count, never also in Assignment_Count (mutually exclusive, no double counting). Verify how the Canvas API distinguishes quizzes (e.g. is_quiz_assignment flag or separate quiz listing) and recommend the reliable counting method.
   - Also gather each course's short name WITHOUT the semester suffix (e.g. for code "CS101-2014J" the name should be like "CS101" or whatever the base name is — explore how course names are stored to determine the short name).

2) Google Form creation (to be done later by a write-capable agent): Create a Google Form titled "Fall 2014 End-of-Semester Student Feedback" with exactly 5 questions:
   Q1: "Which course are you providing feedback for?" — multiple choice, options = all seven Fall 2014 courses in "Course_Code: Course_Name" format.
   Q2: "Overall course satisfaction (1-5)" — multiple choice, options 1 through 5.
   Q3: "What did you like most about the course?" — free text.
   Q4: "What could be improved?" — free text.
   Q5: "Would you recommend this course to others?" — multiple choice, options Yes, No, Maybe.

3) Excel report (to be done later): Create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-feedback/workspace/Fall_2014_Course_Report.xlsx with a single sheet named "Course Statistics" with columns: Course_Code, Course_Name, Enrollment, Avg_Score, Assignment_Count, Quiz_Count, Total_Assessments. Avg_Score rounded to 2 decimals; Total_Assessments = Assignment_Count + Quiz_Count; rows sorted alphabetically by Course_Code; Course_Name = short name without semester suffix.

YOUR JOB: Use your read-only tools to explore the Canvas environment (list courses, check course codes, sample enrollments/assignments/quizzes/submissions/grades structure) enough to:
   - Confirm how many Fall 2014 courses exist and identify them.
   - Confirm the reliable way to compute enrollment count, average student score, assignment count vs quiz count (no double-counting), and the short course name.
   - Identify any pitfalls (e.g. pagination, submission types, quiz assignment duplication, students with zero graded submissions, null scores, ungraded submissions).

Then return a plan with ordered subtasks, each specifying: dispatch decision (self / explore / coder), whether it is parallelizable or must wait on another subtask's output, and the concrete tool calls / verification steps for it. Keep it concise and actionable. Also state the identified list of Fall 2014 courses and their codes if you find them.
Plan Fall 2014 wrap-up task

You are a coder sub-agent gathering statistics for ONE Fall 2014 course in a Canvas LMS (the Canvas MCP tools are available to you: mcp__canvas__canvas_*). The course_id you own is: 2. This is part of a batch of 7 Fall 2014 courses (course codes end with "2014J"); you only handle course 2.

GOAL: Compute and return a compact JSON of course statistics. Follow these steps precisely:

1. COURSE INFO: Call mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course(course_id=2). Record: name, course_code, total_students. The SHORT NAME = name with the trailing " (Fall 2014)" removed (e.g. "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)" → "Applied Analytics & Algorithms").

2. ENROLLMENT: Call mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=2, type=["StudentEnrollment"], per_page=100, page=1), then keep paging (page=2, 3, ...) until pagination.has_more == false. Count ALL returned student enrollments regardless of enrollment_state (do NOT filter to "active" — completed students count toward enrollment). Enrollment = total count. Record the set of all enrolled user_ids.

3. QUIZZES: Call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quizzes(course_id=2). Quiz_Count = length of the returned list. Record each quiz's id and its assignment_id (if present).

4. ASSIGNMENTS: Call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignments(course_id=2). Assignment_Count = number of assignments whose submission_types does NOT contain "online_quiz". VERIFY no double counting: every quiz's assignment_id from step 3 must appear in the assignment list with submission_types containing "online_quiz" (and if any quiz-linked assignment is missing from the list, note it). Quizzes count ONLY in Quiz_Count, never in Assignment_Count.

5. SUBMISSIONS & AVG SCORE: Call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=2, per_page=100, page=1), then keep paging until pagination.has_more == false (use student_ids=["all"] default; this is the bulk submissions endpoint). For each submission record:
   - Use ONLY the raw "score" field. Do NOT normalize by points_possible, do NOT use current_score/final_score fields.
   - If score is non-null (a number, including 0.0), attribute it to that submission's user_id. Keep legitimate 0.0 scores (they are graded).
   - If score is null/absent (ungraded), skip it.
   - Quiz submissions appear in this list as submissions of the quiz-linked assignment — INCLUDE their non-null scores (they are part of "all assessments").
   Then: per-student mean = mean of that student's non-null scores. Avg_Score = mean of the per-student means across all students who have AT LEAST ONE non-null score, rounded to 2 decimal places (round half up). Students with zero non-null scores (including enrolled students who never appear in submissions) are EXCLUDED from this average.
   Also compute: num_students_with_graded_scores (denominator used), num_students_no_graded_scores (enrolled students excluded), sum_of_per_student_means (sum over included students).

6. Total_Assessments = Assignment_Count + Quiz_Count.

7. VERIFICATION: (a) Enrollment should equal the course's total_students field — report both. (b) Assignment_Count + Quiz_Count should equal the total number of assignments returned by list_assignments — report both. (c) Sanity-check your Avg_Score by manually recomputing the per-student means for at least 3 students from the submission data you fetched.

RETURN (compact, valid JSON only, no prose):
{"course_id": ..., "course_code": "...", "short_name": "...", "total_students_field": ..., "enrollment": ..., "num_students_with_graded_scores": ..., "num_students_no_graded_scores": ..., "sum_of_per_student_means": ..., "avg_score": ..., "assignment_count": ..., "quiz_count": ..., "total_assessments": ..., "verification": {"enrollment_matches_total_students": true/false, "assignments_plus_quizzes_matches_assignments_list": true/false, "notes": "..."}}

Work autonomously. Use read-only Canvas tools only (you are not creating anything). If a paginated call fails, retry once; if it still fails, record the error in verification.notes and continue with what you have.
